claims.statement: For every nonempty ordinary arity-2,3,4 path-star profile, with W[k]=Σ_i r_i A_i[k] retaining original private-tip multiplicities and C=G∏_i B_{r_i}, integer-zero-extended coefficients satisfy W[k+1]C[k−1]≤W[k]C[k] for every natural k with 1≤k and 2k≤N+2.
claims.scope: Exact registered guarded weighted-tip-deck comparison on all nonempty ordinary path-stars with m≥1 and r_i∈{2,3,4}; no selector, first-descent or payment conclusion is part of this inequality itself. No guarded counterexample or universal proof was found. The all-rank witness at (a2,a3,a4)=(38,0,1), k=77 lies outside the guard.
claims.reason: 178 authorized input bytes matched their manifests/packet hashes. Exact producer replay and independent exact guarded boundary/interior checks found no failure, but they are finite and do not prove the universal claim.

claims.statement: Conditionally, if the registered weighted shifted comparison holds at guarded k=p, then at every actual eligible lower-half p at least one original branch i has strict current-p selector Δ_p A_i<0.
claims.scope: For the same nonempty ordinary path-star family, use the actual least strict parent descent x (including terminal differences, with flats not descents), all guards x+2≤p, 3p<2(N+2)+1 and 2p≤N+2, and selectors evaluated at current p. Coefficients are integer-zero-extended. Each original private tip retains multiplicity r_i. This is conditional on the weighted inequality, not an unconditional selector theorem; no endpoint selection is implied.
claims.reason: The exact algebra is valid: the registered first-descent ratio-band plus log-concavity gives 0<C[p]/C[p−1]<1; dividing the nonnegative weighted margin by the positive W[p]C[p−1] preserves order and forces Δ_pW<0. Positive r_i then force at least one Δ_pA_i<0.

claims.statement: Conditionally on the weighted shifted comparison at every guarded rank, the actual eligible selected tip set is nonempty and the registered all-m branchwise three-halves bound implies A=Σ_i r_i e_i T_i[j]≥bδD_j, including a possibly selected endpoint tag.
claims.scope: Ordinary path-stars with m≥1, r_i∈{2,3,4}; actual first strict parent descent x, current-p strict selectors and all three lower-half guards retained. Let S=Σ_i r_i e_i. Weighted selector implication gives S≥2; the registered bound 2T_i[j]≥3δD_j for every branch gives A≥(3/2)SδD_j≥(S+e₀)δD_j=bδD_j since e₀∈{0,1}. Original tag multiplicities are retained. This is conditional and does not itself prove the weighted comparison or assert a formal award.
claims.reason: The composition is an exact arithmetic consequence of the weighted selector lemma and the registered all-m branchwise three-halves theorem: S≥2 and e₀≤1 imply 3S/2≥S+e₀.

limitations: No universal proof or guarded counterexample was found for the weighted shifted deck comparison; finite exact checks are bounded evidence only.
The tip-selection and selected-MASS consequences are conditional on the weighted comparison; the MASS composition additionally uses the registered all-m branchwise three-halves result.
No Lean build or formal award was attempted.
